findings.issue: STACK_BUDGET's shares (phone 0.45, tablet 0.3, laptop 0.4, desktop 0.25) are stated once and the class is derived from the size, as asked, but nothing beside the constant says where any share comes from. The comment gives an intent ('a laptop or tablet may wrap the filter bar ... onto a second row'), and a tablet getting a smaller share than a laptop is left unexplained. Measured in this review (new renders, both fonts), the margin at the tightest cell of each class is: phone 27px (844x390, 148/175), laptop 37px (1024x768 demo-large, 270/307), tablet 52px (834x1194, 306/358), desktop 56px (1920x1080 Verdana demo-large, 214/270). That is roughly one control row everywhere. So the budget was not tuned to the pixel, but the headroom is something the reader has to re-measure, not something the code states.
findings.resolution: State the basis beside STACK_BUDGET as a rule the shares follow, e.g. the stack a class is designed to draw in the wide font plus one bar row, and say which cell is each class's tightest. Or derive each share from that rule so the numbers are not free constants.

findings.issue: The docstring of _global_filter_row, the function this diff edits, still says 'this row stays one line'. The diff makes the same row wrap onto rows by design (.gfrange, shell.css's new comment: 'Where its controls do not fit one row they wrap onto rows with a gap'), so the docstring now claims the opposite of what the code does.
findings.resolution: Reword it to say the row wraps onto rows with a gap, with the date range wrapping as one item, and that its cost is held by the pinned-stack budget.

intent.note: Clause 1 ('The matrix stops asserting "one line" anywhere ... (a) no horizontal overflow and nothing clipped; (b) ... a stated budget per viewport class ... stated ONCE as a named constant ... derived from the viewport list; (c) no control or chip wraps inside a word; (d) the counter stays inside its bar. Remove the one-line assertions and say in the matrix's comment why'). The diff removes the old lm3/lm4/lm5 line expects (barLines/rowLines and the 'at most N line(s)' / 'filter row is one line' expects). It adds lm8 (spill, cut-off fields, page width), lm4 against STACK_BUDGET with viewportClass(size, phone) and a by-name FAIL for a class no size reaches, lm5 (word split via per-word rects), lm3 (count rects inside the bar's content box), and the 'WHY NO CELL COUNTS LINES' comment: matches. The only other line-shaped assertions left in the checker are pre-existing and not about chrome rows (the hostile-row 'height > 120' painted probe). Clause 2 ('flex-wrap + row-gap from tokens ... breakpoints ... carry headroom ... must not sit at the edge of one font's width'). The diff gives .toolbar gap var(--sp-1) with flex-wrap; .gfilters gap var(--sp-1), whose row gap was raw .3rem; a new .gfrange that wraps the date pair, its scope and All time as one item; the compaction media query moved from (52rem < width <= 64rem) to (52rem < width < 70rem) with a dated Verdana measurement (row 916-924px vs 1057px at 70rem, about 12.6% spare); and #audit-q's floor in ch (16ch + 2*--sp-2 in border-box, so 16ch-2px of content for the 15-glyph 'Filter by text…'), which scales with the drawn font. That is a design, not a one-value nudge: matches. Clause 3 ('SECOND pass, by default (no flag needed) ... Verdana; fall back ... SAY which font each pass used ... if no wide font is installed, the pass reports that it could not run, it never passes silently ... "wide font" label'). The pass runs by default inside the plain `node tools/check-report-interactive.mjs <file>` call, which is the task gate's own call. It injects addStyleTag(':root,*,*::before,*::after{font-family:"Verdana",sans-serif!important}'), labels cells ` [wide font: Verdana]`, verifies the drawn family via CDP, and prints 'layout matrix fonts: page's own font (.SF NS); wide font Verdana (Verdana)' on the summary line. NOT RUN (none installed, or none wider than the page's own font) is a PASS: exit 0, an 'ok' note, and the reason on the summary line. Its FEATURE_ABSENT row excuses only the font-identity expect. For a gate that is the right call: where it triggers, the first pass already draws in the widest available font, which is the runner's case. On macOS Verdana always ships, so the local gate always runs it; an exit-code-only reader cannot see a NOT RUN, which is accepted, not flagged. Matches. Clause 4 ('the NEW checker run over the a936cc11 renders ... must FAIL in the wide pass at lm5 834x1194 and at lm4 1024x768 on demo-large, as CI did; and ... must PASS over your new renders'). Re-run by me: git show a936cc11: acme -> rc=1, 'REPORT IS INERT: 56 interaction(s)', every FAIL lm8, including 'FAIL lm8 1024x768 [wide font: Verdana] View=active at rest: ... cut off: #audit-q placeholder 227px in 197px; page 1009px on a 1024px screen; top bar 122px'. git show a936cc11: demo-large -> rc=1, 56 FAIL, all lm8, including 'FAIL lm8 834x1194 [wide font: Verdana] View=active at rest: ... cut off: #audit-q placeholder 227px in 214px; page 819px on a 834px screen; top bar 151px' and the same at 1024x768. Working-tree acme -> rc=0 'report is interactive: 848 checks passed'; demo-large -> rc=0 '854 checks passed'; both print 'layout matrix fonts: page's own font (.SF NS); wide font Verdana (Verdana)'. The old renders go red at the clause's cells through lm8 (search placeholder cut off), not through a budget breach: old demo-large wide lm4 is 'ok ... 295px against 358px' at 834x1194 and 'ok ... 262px against 307px' at 1024x768. That follows from clause 1 (the extra row is allowed by design), and the executor said so plainly. Two facts give real evidence that the wide pass stands in for the runner. First, the wide pass on the old demo-large render reproduces CI's own figures exactly: top bar 151px at 834x1194 and filter bar 92.0px at 1024x768, against CI's 'top bar 151px' and '(2 lines; 92px)'. Second, at 1512x945 and 1920x1080 on acme the old render fails only in the wide pass. Claim vs diff: the outcome describes the diff accurately (STACK_BUDGET values, viewportClass thresholds, WIDE_FONTS, .gfrange, the 70rem bound, the placeholder change, the dropped 9rem select cap). One mismatch: casesAdded lists is1-is10, .dtoggle, .shacopy and tr. These interaction-state probes exist unchanged at a936cc11 (`git show a936cc11:tools/check-report-interactive.mjs | grep -c "id: 'is[0-9]"` = 10; the diff adds 0), so they answer tests.add but were not added by this task.
